rites.name: Valaulium
rites.text: Valaulium is the concept of the Singing in Drore, the sound that rings through the world as its first roots take hold in the earth. It is remembered in the groves as the force that made the soil hold together and the first kingdoms possible.

rites.name: Ukamasanari
rites.text: Ukamasanari is the concept of a sound that lets the first roots of Drore condense out of silence, felt as a low hum that settles into the ground. During the Age of Strangers it was the bond outsiders traded for, a pledge that a newcomer would be held by the land they sang into.

rites.name: Sheistezora
rites.text: Sheistezora is the concept of a quiet, unsung stretch of Drore's making, when the makers plant the Weave and the hidden powers lie dormant beneath the surface of things. It is remembered as a time of patient sowing rather than of loud deeds, when small threads were pulled taut across the land.

rites.name: Xaithess
rites.text: Xaithess is a concept held in the Drore archive, a shape of possibility that the Library files whenever a future splits into branches. In the early Age of the first sovereign, it is invoked by groves and growing kingdoms to decide which harvests and treaties will take root.

rites.name: Kraikurn
rites.text: Kraikurn is a concept within the Drore universe, a notion held in the Grounded Realm during Era E7 that governs how powers are understood and taught. It belongs to the Holy Age, when flame, temples and orders shaped every practice, and its teachers reckoned a power by the vows that bound it. Scholars of the Three Futures shelved it as a rule for what a power may do rather than as a force in itself.

rites.name: Ryaruanwen
rites.text: Ryaruanwen is a concept in the Drore cycle, drawn from the moment the Three Futures split and the Library begins shelving every possible ending. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, it is remembered as the idea that a single kindled lamp can outlast the wick that fed it.
